d.d: The ma'oma'o, Gymnomyza samoensis, a large passerine bird native to Samoa.

A fairy chess piece which moves identically to the xiangqi horse, moving one square orthogonally and then one square diagonally at a 135 degree angle. Similar to the chess knight, but has more limited movement as its movement can be obstructed by an intervening piece.
A card game, named after Mao Zedong, in which players attempt to shed all their cards without violating certain unspoken rules.
A branch of the Omotic languages spoken in Ethiopia.
The philosophy espoused by Chinese leader Mao Zedong, a form of Marxism-Leninism that focuses on the peasantry as the revolutionary vanguard.
of, related to, or advocating Maoism
A member of the indigenous people of New Zealand.
A member of the indigenous people of the Cook Islands.
Of, from, or pertaining to the Māori.
